title: Spain Train Crash: 17 Minutes After the Order #Shorts
description:
At least 68 people died on Wednesday 28 Oct 2026 when a Renfe high-speed train hit the back of a stopped Iryo train in Toledo province, Spain. The LZB safety system had failed about 20 minutes earlier, and reports say the train was ordered to resume about 17 minutes before impact. The transport minister called it "inexplicable". A court and Spain's rail accident investigators are examining what happened; nothing is concluded yet.
Sources: CNN, CBC, ABC News, NPR, CBS, SBS.
Footage: stock clips for illustration (Pixabay), not of the actual event. Hosts are AI-generated; script fact-checked.
Subscribe for the day's news explained in a minute.

CAST: Arjun (calm explainer) and Meera (warm, quiet journalist), fixed reference photos, neutral muted studio. No other characters. Sombre tone, no graphic imagery, no logos, soft low music, no SFX.

SCRIPT (~52s):
ARJUN: "About seventeen minutes. That's how long a high-speed train ran after being told to resume, with Spain's safety system still down."
MEERA: "At least 68 people died on Wednesday when a Renfe AVE high-speed train hit the back of a stopped Iryo train in Toledo province, Spain. More than 500 people were on board. Dozens more are in hospital."
ARJUN: "Around 8:30 a.m., a computer failure knocked out the LZB train safety system along about 63 kilometres of track. Six trains stopped."
MEERA: "Then, according to reports of the ministry's reconstruction, the Renfe train was ordered to resume at about 8:36. The collision came at around 8:53."
ARJUN: "Transport Minister Óscar Puente says the control centre let traffic resume without the system restored, while a stop signal was still active. He called it 'inexplicable'. He says the drivers are not to blame: 'I am not attributing responsibility to anyone, I am just stating the facts.'"
MEERA: "A court in Orgaz and Spain's rail accident investigators are examining what happened. The black boxes have been seized. Nothing has been concluded. It is Spain's second deadly high-speed rail disaster this year, after Adamuz in January."
MEERA: "Our thoughts are with the families. Should trains ever run at normal speed when the safety system is down?"
